title: Secure Email Gateway
summary: A secure email gateway is the control point that inspects mail as it crosses the boundary of an organisation, applying policy before messages reach user mailboxes and controlling outbound traffic as well. It typically terminates the connection, then layers checks: sender authentication results such as SPF, DKIM and DMARC, reputation and blocklist lookups, content and attachment analysis, sandbox detonation of links and files, URL rewriting so clicks are rechecked at the moment of use, data loss prevention rules for outbound mail, and encryption for messages that must not travel in plain text. Most deployments sit in front of the mailbox service, either as an on-premises appliance or a cloud service, and the mailbox platform is then locked so mail can only arrive through the gateway. Detection quality depends on tuning, because aggressive blocking creates false positives that push users to bypass the filter with personal accounts. The mistake people usually make is treating the gateway as a complete solution, then leaving the mailbox able to accept direct connections, which lets an attacker skip the gateway entirely.

beginner.definition: A secure email gateway is a filter that all company email passes through. It checks each message and its attachments before delivery. It can block, quarantine or clean suspicious mail. It also applies rules to mail that your staff send out.
beginner.whyItMatters: Most attacks arrive by email, often as a fake invoice or a file that asks to be opened. A gateway stops many of these messages before a person ever sees them. It also protects your secrets from leaving in an outgoing message. Good filtering reduces the number of risky decisions your busy staff must make. It is not perfect, so users still need training.
howItWorks: Mail for your domain is directed to the gateway instead of going straight to mailboxes.
The gateway checks whether the sender passes authentication and reputation checks.
It scans the body, links and attachments, and can open files in a safe sandbox.
Suspicious links are rewritten, then rechecked when a user actually clicks them.
Messages that fail policy are blocked, quarantined or marked with a warning.
Outgoing mail is checked against rules so private data does not leave the company.
beginner.example: Think of the mailroom clerk at a large hospital. Every parcel is opened at the desk and checked before it reaches a ward. Fluids and unknown powders are held back. The clerk also reads outgoing post to make sure patient papers are not sent by mistake. The wards never receive parcels directly, because that would skip the check.
takeaways: Lock the mailbox service so all mail must pass through the gateway.
Tune filters carefully, because false positives make users look for ways around them.
A gateway reduces risk but cannot replace user awareness and reporting.

objectives: Explain what a secure email gateway does and where it sits in the mail path.
Describe the main inspection layers, including authentication checks, content scanning and sandboxing.
Explain why URL rewriting and click-time checking add value over a single scan.
Recognise how outbound filtering and data loss prevention rules protect the organisation.
Identify configuration mistakes that let attackers bypass the gateway completely.
